newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-SMITH ORDERED TO STAY WITH QUEENSLAND.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SMITH ORDERED TO STAY WITH QUEENSLAND.

text.p: Australia test winger Damian Smith has been refused permission to break his contract with Queensland to play for New South Wales in the southern hemisphere provincial Super 12 tournament this season.
But he will be free to represent New South Wales in the competition in 1998 after the Australian Rugby Union (ARU) ruled that he should be released from the two-year contract 12 months early.
The ruling body intervened in the dispute between the two state unions when Queensland refused Smith's request for an immediate move after he began pre-season training with New South Wales.
Smith must honour the terms of his contract with Queensland until after their fixture against France on June 17, ARU spokesman Greg Thomas said on Saturday.
"Damian had a two-year contract and it was shortened by a year," Thomas said.
"There was a contract in place and it would have set a precedent if this was broken. It's very important that the contract remains," he added.
